images.title: Parthiv's matchstick Ls
images.purpose: Show that every L uses 2 matchsticks, so the sticks are 2 times the number of Ls.
images.composition: Three Ls stand in a row across the middle of the frame with a brace below them; one short caption sits beneath; wide white space.
exact_structure: Exactly 3 identical L shapes stand side by side with equal gaps, each made of 2 matchsticks: one upright stick in teal #0072B2 and one flat stick in amber #E69F00 joined at the bottom left corner; each stick has a small rounded grey #6B7280 head at one end; 6 sticks in all.
Above the first L only, a small text "1 L = 2 sticks".
Under the row, one grey #6B7280 brace spans the 3 Ls with the text "3 Ls" centred below it.
Below the brace, one caption line "3 × 2 = 6 sticks", then a second line "n Ls: 2 × n sticks" with the n in reddish purple #CC79A7.
Nothing else in the frame; no table, no numbers for 5 or 45 Ls.
rejection: a count of Ls other than 3 or of sticks other than 6
an L drawn with more or fewer than 2 sticks
the answers for 5, 7 or 45 Ls shown
a dash or hyphen in the captions
images.takeaway: Every L needs 2 sticks, so n Ls need 2 × n sticks.
images.description: Three matchstick Ls with a brace, the caption 3 × 2 = 6 sticks and the rule n Ls: 2 × n sticks.
images.context: Shown beside the matchstick example text and video.
images.teaching_notes: Count the sticks in one L, then in three Ls, and only then read the rule with n.

image_decisions.why: The matchstick Ls are the first pattern turned into an expression, and seeing 2 sticks per L makes 2 × n obvious.
